subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
solution:
The correct answer is '**truth**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence says that Hollywood directors believed something firmly — this implies a widely accepted belief or principle.
 
• The phrase “accepted as gospel” is an idiom that means something accepted as undeniably true.
 
• "**Truth**" fits best because it aligns with the idiom “gospel truth,” meaning an unquestioned belief.
 
• Other options like "**blasphemy**", "**followers**", and "**Bible**" do not logically fit the idiomatic expression in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel * *truth__* * that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a ____at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which **________****every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful **_________****on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this **_________****in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Blasphemy: Refers to profane talk about sacred things — not suitable here.
 
• Followers: Refers to people — doesn't fit grammatically or contextually.
 
• Bible: While "gospel" relates to the Bible, using “Bible” after it would be redundant and awkward.
